Contribution 1: compute-optimal scaling analysis — authors revisit the question of how to trade off model size and training tokens given a fixed FLOPs budget; they estimate N_opt(C) and D_opt(C) from over 400 models ranging from under 70M to over 16B parameters, trained on 5B to over 400B tokens. Their conclusion: model size and training tokens should be scaled in roughly equal proportions, in contrast to Kaplan et al. (2020) which recommends model size increase 5.5× and tokens only 1.8× per 10× compute increase. Aliases: E016, E018, E021, E004, E043, E045.

Contribution 2: three approaches — Approach 1 (fix model sizes, vary tokens), Approach 2 (IsoFLOP profiles), Approach 3 (parametric loss fitting). Predictions comparable: a=0.50/0.49/0.46 and b=0.50/0.51/0.54; Kaplan et al. 0.73/0.27 (E122, E123). Aliases: E056, E066, E084, E107, E122, E123.

Contribution 3: Chinchilla — a 70B model trained on 1.4T tokens with the same FLOPs as Gopher (280B), outperforming Gopher across evaluation suites: MMLU 67.6% vs 60.0% (E176, E182), Pile bpb on all subsets (E173), BIG-bench 65.1% vs 54.4% (E187), reading comprehension LAMBADA 77.4 vs 74.5, RACE (E185), closed-book QA (E209), common sense (E202). Also 4× smaller reduces inference cost (E140).
